reports.title: Fervo Energy Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results

guidance.heading: outlook.
section: •Ended Q3 2026 with unrestricted cash and cash equivalents of $1.9 billion and current and long-term debt of

desk.headline: First geothermal plant online and Google deal signed; tiny revenue missed, H2 capex cut on timing

other.label: Contracted capacity
other.change: vs 658 MW at end of Q2

results: Cape Station GeoBlock 1 (33 MW) began commercial operation on 30 Sep, ahead of its contract date; revenue was only $116k.
Loss to common shareholders was $20.8m ($0.07 a share), better than the $0.10 loss expected.
Reported net income of $11.7m was lifted by a $29.9m tax benefit and an $11.8m swap gain.
Administrative costs rose to $39.4m from $27.4m in Q2 on share-based pay, listing costs and hiring.
A 396 MW, 15-year supply deal with Google lifted contracted revenue to about $11.9bn.

guidance.summary: Fervo cut its second-half 2026 capital spending forecast to $700–750m from $850–900m, saying some spending moves later with no change to timelines or total cost. Q4 and 2027 revenue outlooks are unchanged.

points: GeoBlock 1 output and power deliveries are meeting expectations; GeoBlocks 2 and 3 are due online by 1 Jan 2027.
Cape Google 400 total investment of about $2.2bn is unchanged, targeting $5,500 per kW versus about $7,000 for Phase I.
Project financing for Cape Google 400 could come around mid-2027 at about 70% loan-to-value.
A 600 MW expansion option with Google depends on regulatory progress for direct supply to a data centre.
Risks flagged: heat decline seen at the earlier Project Red site, and a planned third-party substation outage.
call.source: Call coverage — Zacks Equity Research, 10 Nov 2026

watch: GeoBlocks 2 and 3 reaching commercial operation by 1 Jan 2027, completing about 100 MW.
Q4 revenue, the first full quarter of power sales from Cape Station.
Drilling progress and costs at Cape Google 400 against the $5,500 per kW target.
